fact_check.claim: Kaspa went on a really nice ride, 5 cents is the resistance level where the sell orders sit, if it breaks it goes to 5.5 cents; Mike would like to wake up and see it broke through 5 cents (transcript, stream of Sept 26)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED to 2026-09-27: $KAS $0.0485, market cap about $1.345B, rank 71, +7.8% 24h, +25.2% 7d, +66.2% 30d (CoinGecko); DiarioBitcoin logged a +17% day on Sept 26 at $0.0468. It has NOT closed above 5 cents at drafting time, so all copy says 'knocking on 5 cents' / 'just under 5 cents', never 'broke 5 cents'; the 5-cent resistance and 5.5-cent next stop are Mike's own levels in first person.
fact_check.source: api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/markets?ids=kaspa (2026-09-27); diariobitcoin.com Kaspa analisis del 26 de septiembre de 2026

fact_check.claim: Kaspa flipped Polygon on market cap (a chat comment Mike confirmed: 'well deserved')
fact_check.verdict: verified on 2026-09-27: Kaspa $1.345B (rank 71) vs POL (Polygon Ecosystem Token) $1.280B (rank 73) on CoinGecko. Copy: 'flipped Polygon ($POL) on market cap this week, about $1.35B vs $1.28B'. 'One of the most VC-backed chains of the last cycle' is general wording (Polygon's 2022 Sequoia-led $450M raise is public record but the number is not used).

fact_check.claim: The first vProg is live on Kaspa testnet ('Big tech toe' = tic-tac-toe), a verifiable program with real execution and real settlement, still a stack of PRs to review and merge, already a working proof of concept, the front end can be enhanced and built separately (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: KuCoin news (2026-09-27, citing @Kaspionkas) 'The first vProg is live on testnet: a fully verifiable tic-tac-toe game with real off-chain execution + on-chain ZK settlement'; the guest program is biryukovmaxim/vprog-tictactoe (stakes locked in a pot, the vProg settles the pot to the winner); public TN10 desk notes record a stress test with vprogs/tic-tac-toe from 25 Sep 20:12 to 26 Sep 13:16 CEST (about 17 hours). Copy: 'tic-tac-toe game with real off-chain execution and zero-knowledge settlement on the Kaspa L1', 'proof of concept, a stack of PRs still to merge', '17-hour stress test on testnet this week'. Testnet only, never described as mainnet.

fact_check.claim: Kaspa does 10 blocks per second (used in copy as context for vProgs)
fact_check.verdict: verified public fact: Kaspa mainnet has run at 10 blocks per second since the Crescendo hard fork (May 2025).
fact_check.source: kaspa.org / Crescendo hard fork coverage, May 2025 (well-established)

fact_check.claim: TAO was pumping too, Mike swing-traded a small bag at about $319 to $327 (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED: $TAO $334.81, +32.5% 7d, +34.9% 30d, market cap about $3.8B (CoinGecko, 2026-09-27). Copy: 'up about 32% on the week to around $335'. The swing trade / profit-taking is trader-portfolio framing (persona no_rotation_framing) and is NOT used; the tweet is the persona core thesis (TAO = neutral AI inference layer, KAS = PoW money layer). The humanoid-robot-shot-by-a-cannon video and the Shenzhen 'robot valley' clip could not be verified and are written only as the general 'robots are going to be everywhere in a couple of years'. persona project_handles tao = null, so no Follow line.

fact_check.claim: 'Graham coin, Graham, or just Graham, ton coin' is pumping (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified: Toncoin was renamed Gram, ticker TON to GRAM, on 2026-06-15 after an 81% community vote (name and ticker change only, network still The Open Network). CoinGecko lists it as Gram: $1.61, +10.2% 24h, +18.2% 7d. Whisper's 'Graham' is Gram. Copy uses '$GRAM' (persona still lists $TON; current reality wins per verified_claims_only). Poll eligibility key stays 'toncoin' (no TON poll drafted this batch).

fact_check.claim: Quant is ripping, Litecoin was about $40 in the bear market and is $71 now, big caps pumping while micro caps have not moved (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED: $QNT $162.92, +54.9% 24h, +157% 7d; $LTC $71.70, +25.9% 7d, +46% 30d (CoinGecko 2026-09-27). Copy uses the weekly percentages only; the '$40 in the bear market' Litecoin number is not used. 'Micro caps have barely moved yet' is Mike's own market read in the thread.

fact_check.claim: Bitcoin dominance is falling off a cliff since June, total market cap excluding the top 10 keeps going up, others dominance just broke through its downtrend resistance, so alt season has started even though Bitcoin only just got above the 50-week moving average (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in general form and UPDATED: Bitcoin dominance fell below 60% in the week ending Sept 26 (58.5% on Sept 26) while $BTC gained; the last break below 60% was September 2025, when the altcoin season index hit 78 on Sept 20 and fell to 14 by Dec 19; seven large alts outran Bitcoin on the week (LTC +23.7% in that count); $2.4B flowed into spot Bitcoin ETFs Sept 21-25. The 'others dominance broke its downtrend' and 'total ex-top-10 keeps climbing' lines are Mike's own chart reads, written as his read. $BTC $84,984, +5.7% 7d (CoinGecko). Copy: 'dropped below 60% this week', '$BTC did about 6%', 'alt season started the same week Bitcoin reclaimed its 50-week SMA'.
fact_check.source: finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-share-crypto-market-drops-170914034.html (2026-09-26); tradingview.com cryptobriefing 'Bitcoin dominance falls below 60%'; api.coingecko.com (bitcoin, 2026-09-27)

fact_check.claim: Bitcoin at about $84,400 needs to hold the May high (about $82,700) into the weekly close, the 50-week moving average is about $77K, and we cannot officially call a bull market until two weekly closes above the 50-week SMA; Benjamin Cowan's 'I am already wrong' video (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED: the Sept 20 weekly close was $81,159, the first close above the 50-week SMA (about $78,788) since Nov 9, 2025; the May 2026 peak was near $82,000; $BTC trades near $85K on 2026-09-27. Because the Sept 27 weekly close is unknown at drafting time and the batch posts days later, no copy predicts or reports that close: the thread states Mike's two-close rule, that the first close printed Sept 20 at $81,159, and that Bitcoin has traded around $85K since. The May-high level is not quoted as a number. Benjamin Cowan's video is not drafted (commentary on another creator's mea culpa).

fact_check.claim: Long-term holders sold the whole way down and now, with price going up, only a small amount are selling; the Bitcoin god candles are buyers offsetting sellers (transcript, on-chain chart shown on stream)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own on-chain chart read, written in first person as his read, no specific figure claimed; the four-year cycle zombie framing follows persona core_theses (their October demand turns October green; never written as the zombies causing an October bottom).

fact_check.claim: Golden Kitty is at $5.3M and Mike thinks it is $8M in a couple of weeks (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED: $GOLDEN $0.00556, market cap about $5.56M, +10.7% 24h, +88% 7d, new ATH $0.00592 on 2026-09-27 (CoinGecko). Copy: 'printed another all-time high this week, up about 88% on the week to a $5.5M cap'; the $8M target is Mike's own call ('my $8M call'). Official X handle is not in persona project_handles, so no Follow line.

fact_check.claim: Kaspa to 50 cents: 'over the next few years, yeah definitely, I think we're going to have 50 cents' (transcript, answering chat)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own forward-looking prediction, written in first person; used as the deliberate engagement-bait one-liner and in the YT post / poll setup.

fact_check.claim: KRC20 days are coming back because Kaspa is getting more popular and vProgs are coming; long road, 2027 or even 2028 (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own thesis, kept as his read with his own years; no KRC20 token is named (the dead 'Knight' token aside is dropped).

fact_check.claim: Dropped from the batch: promo code ARCHIE / 50% off (membership pitch, already shipped in archie-promo); the 110x PerpsPad, 17x and 13x STONK calls (already shipped in perpspad / ready-for-pumps); the What If yacht and Archie bashing (already covered, and a $IF mention would force the Follow line); the October / Pumpkin Halloween memes, Bike Tyson, Swole, Clanker, Bio, Polly, Near, Zeke (unverified small tokens, or a Kaspa fork Mike himself is unsure about; persona verified_claims_only); the Florida property accepting Kaspa (chat comment, unverified); 'the crypto market added $650B in six months' (chat comment, unverified); the US-China tariff and AI hotline headline, Trump rejecting an Iran deal, the 'crypto's biggest mistake' politics thread (political tangents); the YouTube subscriber-count comparison and 'am I being throttled' talk (self-focused); 'maybe I should have gotten into Quant' (self-deprecating framing); the Archetype / Crypto John sold-Kaspa gossip (unverified third parties); Benjamin Cowan commentary; the robotics-stock ad clip (Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Oklo: not Mike's content).
fact_check.verdict: not drafted per persona avoid_in_drafts and the agent instructions (no membership pitches, no re-announcements, no unverified claims, no political tangents, no self-deprecating framing).

fact_check.claim: Housecoin and Pengu on this stream
fact_check.verdict: NOT discussed (Pengu only as 'Polly pays rewards in Pengu', an unverified pairing token), so they carry no weight this batch; the weighting applied is Kaspa first (3 of 6 tweets, the YT post, thread 1, the X poll), then TAO (1 tweet), Gram / Toncoin (inside the alt-season tweet and thread), then Golden Kitty (1 one-liner).

fact_check.claim: Whisper corrections applied: 'Tao' / 'towel' -> TAO; 'Graham' -> Gram ($GRAM); 'Big tech toe' -> tic-tac-toe; 'B-PROG' / 'vprogs' -> vProg / vProgs; 'cell orders' -> sell orders; 'Robert her chain' / 'Robahood' -> Robinhood Chain; 'golden kid' -> Golden Kitty; 'Cass' -> Kaspa (chat shorthand); 'Irish diversions' -> bearish divergences (not used); '50 week moving average' -> 50-week SMA; 'tangent' -> Tangem wallet (not used)

Why I think alt season started early...
tweets.hook: Bitcoin dominance dropped below 60% this week and the alts did not wait for permission.

tweets.text: Bitcoin dominance has been rolling over since June. Total crypto market cap excluding the top 10 keeps climbing week after week, and the dominance of everything outside the top 10 just broke through a downtrend that had held for months.

The weird part: this is happening the same week Bitcoin reclaimed its 50-week SMA (about $78,800) with an $81,159 weekly close on Sept 20, the first close above it since November 2025.

Alt season is not supposed to start this early in the reclaim. It is.

My rule: two weekly closes above the 50-week SMA before I officially call it a bull market. The first printed Sept 20 at $81,159, and $BTC has been trading around $85K since, so I like the odds on the second.

Look at the long-term holders. They sold the whole way down (four-year cycle zombies waiting for an October bottom), and now that price is going up almost nobody is selling. Bitcoin god candles with no sellers on the other side. That is buyers, not zombies.

The last time dominance broke 60% was September 2025 and the alt season index collapsed by December. The difference this time: $2.4B went into spot Bitcoin ETFs in the same week dominance fell, and the big caps ran first. The micro caps from $1M to $500M have barely moved yet.

If this made the alt season read click...

yt_posts.body_style: news stack: the three-piece week in the pre-fold hook, the chart and the 5-cent resistance, the Polygon flip, the vProg proof of concept and the stress test, what vProgs are and why they change the chain, the long-road KRC20 and 50-cent read, a forked price-target question and a like/subscribe ask tied to the coming vProgs video
yt_posts.body:
Kaspa flipped Polygon on market cap, printed a 66% month, and the first vProg went live on testnet. All in the same week.

I have been making Kaspa videos through the whole bear market. This is the week the chain and the chart finally started moving together, and here is what each piece actually means.

The chart first. $KAS is up about 25% on the week and about 66% on the month, sitting just under 5 cents. I have said for a while that 5 cents is where the sell orders are stacked; it is a resistance level, and if it breaks, 5.5 cents is the next stop. On the way up, $KAS passed Polygon ($POL) on market cap, about $1.35B vs $1.28B. A fair-launch proof-of-work DAG with no premine and no VC cap table just passed one of the most VC-backed chains of the last cycle. Well deserved.

Now the part that matters more than the price. The first vProg is live on Kaspa testnet: a tic-tac-toe game with real off-chain execution and zero-knowledge settlement on the L1. It is a proof of concept, there is a stack of PRs still to review and merge, and the front end is basic and gets built separately. But it runs, and it ran through a 17-hour stress test on testnet this week.

vProgs are verifiable programs. The app runs off-chain and proves itself back to the Kaspa L1, a proof-of-work DAG doing 10 blocks per second. Anybody can build on it. That is Kaspa going from 'fast payments coin' to a chain that can do anything the other chains do, and I am planning a full video on it.

Here is my read on the long road. Remember the KRC20 days? They are coming back, bigger, because once apps live on the L1 every Kaspa token gets a reason to exist again. It is not going to be 2026; it could be 2027, it could be 2028. You stick with it, and the portfolio keeps growing. And yes, I still think 50 cents happens over the next few years.

So commit in the comments: where does $KAS top out THIS bull run: under 25 cents, 25 to 50 cents, 50 cents to a dollar, or higher?

Click that like button and click the subscribe button if you want the vProgs deep dive when it drops.
